newsitem.title: USA: ALPINE SKIING-WIBERG, MAGONI SHARE VICTORY IN WOMEN'S SLALOM.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-WIBERG, MAGONI SHARE VICTORY IN WOMEN'S SLALOM.

text.p: Overall champion Pernilla Wiberg of Sweden and Lara Magoni of Italy finished in a dead heat in Sunday's slalom to share victory in the last race of the women's Alpine skiing World Cup season.
Wiberg, fifth after the first run and 0.76 of a second behind pace-setter Magoni, blistered the 55-gate course with a sizzling second run of 48.30 seconds to jump into the lead.

Magoni, the silver medallist in slalom at the Sestriere world championships, rose to the occasion as the last racer down the mountain by clocking 49.06 for a combined time of one minute, 35.77 seconds to tie slalom champion Wiberg for first.
Katja Seizinger of Germany finished third, 0.54 of a second behind the co-winners.
Fourth place went to Ingrid Salvenmoser of Austria in 1:36.97, followed by Norway's Trine Bakke and World Cup giant slalom champion Deborah Compagnoni of Italy in sixth.
New Zealander Claudia Riegler, winner of three slaloms this season, held on to second place ahead of Compagnoni in the season slalom standings by finishing ninth in 1:37.72.
